name: Port and Station District
tagline: Where the ferries to the art islands leave from
description: The area around Takamatsu station and the Sunport ferry terminal, with the piers for Naoshima, Teshima and Shodoshima, the hotels and the covered arcades running south from it. This is the practical base for anyone whose reason to be here is the Setouchi islands.
bestFor: Anyone using Takamatsu as the mainland base for the art islands
pros: Ferries to the art islands from the doorstep
Station, buses and the arcades all close
cons: The highest rents in the city

name: Ritsurin and the Southern Centre
tagline: Around the garden, quiet and green
description: The district around Ritsurin Garden, one of the finest strolling gardens in Japan, laid out over a century against a wooded hill that forms part of the composition. The streets around it are residential and calm, with the private railway and the JR line both close and the centre a short ride north.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting the garden as the daily walk
pros: Ritsurin Garden at the end of the street
Two rail lines into the centre
cons: Ten minutes from the port and the arcades
Garden entry is charged, so daily visits add up

name: Marugamemachi and the Arcades
tagline: Under the covered shopping streets, the longest in the country
description: Takamatsu's covered arcades run for two and a half kilometres, the longest continuous stretch in Japan, and the districts along them hold the shops, the izakaya and much of the city's apartment stock. Living here means the whole centre is reachable without ever being rained on.
bestFor: Anyone who wants everything reachable under cover
pros: The whole centre accessible without weather
cons: Some arcade sections have empty units

name: Yashima and the Eastern Suburbs
tagline: Below the lava plateau, with the view over the Inland Sea
description: The eastern districts below Yashima, a flat-topped lava plateau that rises above the coast and gives the best view over the Seto Inland Sea and its islands. Residential and quiet, with the private railway running out to it and rents well below the centre.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting the sea view and lower rents
pros: Yashima plateau and its views on the doorstep
Rents well below the city centre
Quiet residential streets by the coast
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes into the centre
Few restaurants and little going on
Requires the private line or a car

name: Naoshima and the Art Islands (by ferry)
tagline: The Benesse islands, an hour out on the Inland Sea
description: The islands off Takamatsu that hold the Setouchi art project: Naoshima with the Chichu and Lee Ufan museums and the Art House projects, Teshima with its concrete shell, Inujima with the converted copper refinery. Ferries run from Takamatsu port. Accommodation on the islands is limited and books out.
bestFor: Short island stays rather than a base, given the limited accommodation
pros: Some of the most significant contemporary art installations anywhere
Quiet island life once the day-trippers leave
Cycling is the way to get around Naoshima
cons: Very little accommodation and it books far ahead
Museums close on Mondays and in winter periods
